rejected_rule.statement: A defined track must be used for over ten years to establish a right of way by prescription, and the substitution of one track for another does not apply in cases where a servitude is claimed by virtue of prescriptive user.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: It is a prerequisite to the acquisition of a right of way by prescription that a well-defined and identifiable course or track should have been adversely used by the owner of the dominant tenement for over ten years. ... If a new track is substituted for another, it must, in the absence of a notarial grant, be used for the full prescriptive period before any servitude in respect of it can be established.
